================================================================================
Iowa HHS — Iowa Respiratory Virus Surveillance Report
MMWR Week 40, October 2, 2022 - October 8, 2022 (Season 2022-2023)
Source: https://publications.iowa.gov/41823/1/422f3973-999c-4e8d-9e07-584b7cf9ff47.pdf
================================================================================

Note: Published by the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services. Summaries
of each surveillance section, excluding the cover page and the "About the Data"
methods section. Figures and embedded data values are described in prose.


================ SECTION: International Influenza Activity (WHO) and National Influenza-Like Illness (CDC) ================
The WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS/FluNet) map, generated 30 September 2022, displays the percentage of respiratory specimens testing positive for influenza by transmission zone, with pie charts indicating subtype mix (A H1N1 pdm09, A H3, A not subtyped, and B). Notable early-season activity appears across the tropical and southern hemisphere zones, including parts of Africa, South Asia, and Oceania showing >20% positivity, while most northern hemisphere zones (including North America) showed low positivity (0-10%) consistent with off-season timing. The CDC ILINet activity map for the 2022-23 season, week 40 ending October 8, 2022, classified most U.S. states as Minimal or Low; Georgia and South Carolina registered High activity, Texas and the District of Columbia were Moderate to High, and scattered states (Louisiana, New York City) showed Moderate, signaling early influenza activity emerging in the U.S. Southeast.

================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Survey - Influenza ================
Iowa influenza activity was Low at week 40 (week ending 10/8/2022), the start of the 2022-2023 season. The molecular testing chart shows a single early-season bar of roughly 3,000 tests with near-0% positivity, and the antigen chart shows about 177 tests with low positivity; both series are otherwise empty as the season has just begun. The cover Quick Stats list overall molecular Flu positive at 0.1% and antigen at 1.7%. The current-week regional table reports total molecular positivity of 0.0% Flu A and 0.0% Flu B across 3,266 tests, and antigen Flu A positivity of 1.7% across 177 tests. Region 6-E performed the most molecular tests (2,356), followed by 1-C (749); molecular Flu B reached 0.8% in 2-NE (124 tests). For antigen, 2-NE had the highest Flu A positivity at 10.0% (10 tests) and 6-E at 9.5% (21 tests), while 1-C (78 tests) and 5-SE (62 tests) were 0.0%.

================ SECTION: Influenza Testing at the State Hygienic Laboratory (SHL) ================
Cumulative influenza viruses detected by SHL by age group (10/3/2021 - current week) totaled just 1 Influenza A detection (A not subtyped, in the 50-64 age group) and 0 Influenza B (B Victoria, B Yamagata, and B not subtyped all 0), reflecting the very start of the new surveillance season. All other age groups (unknown, 65 and over, 5-17, 25-49, 18-24, 0-4) reported 0 across both A subtypes (A H1N1 pdm09, A H3, A variant) and B lineages. The weekly stacked chart shows a single early-season bar of 1 positive (A not subtyped, orange) near November 2022 with no other detections plotted. The predominant flu type at SHL on the cover was reported as "A not subtyped." Cell counts of three or fewer are sometimes suppressed for confidentiality.

================ SECTION: Outpatient Health Care Provider Surveillance Program (ILINet) ================
Outpatient ILI activity was low at the start of the season. The seasonal ILI chart shows the 2022-23 curve (dark red) beginning near baseline, with the week ending 10/8/2022 marked at 1.1% ILI; prior seasons peaked much higher (the 2021-22 curve, teal, spiked above 10% late in its season). The ILI Recent Weeks table shows rising activity: Week 38 (9/24/2022) 22 total ILI at 0.44%, Week 39 (10/1/2022) 27 at 0.58%, and Week 40 (10/8/2022) 48 total ILI at 1.09% (matching the cover Quick Stat of 1.09%). The current-week age distribution was concentrated in ages 5-24 (17) and 25-49 (13) and 0-4 (12), with 50-64 at 2 and 65 and older at 4.

================ SECTION: Influenza and COVID-19 Hospitalizations - HealthData.gov ================
Influenza hospitalizations were essentially absent at the start of the season. The "Influenza Hospitalizations by Week - HHS Protect" chart (scaled 0-6) shows no plotted bars for the period, indicating zero weekly flu hospitalizations entering October 2022. The Iowa Sentinel Site Survey for influenza-associated hospitalizations (10/2/2022 - 10/8/2022) reported 0 across every age group: 0-4 (0), 5-24 (0), 25-49 (0), 50-64 (0), 65+ (0), and Unknown Age (0). This is consistent with the cover Quick Stats reporting a sentinel rate of 0/10,000 and 5 flu hospitalizations across all Iowa hospitals for the week, with 0 cumulative flu deaths across all ages.

================ SECTION: School Illness Reporting ================
School illness was low at week 40. The sentinel-school chart shows the 2022-23 percent-absent curve (purple) beginning the season, with the week ending 10/8/2022 marked at 2.5% absent due to illness, in range of prior early-season values; the 2021-22 curve (teal) had peaked above 6% earlier in its season. The county map of "Numbers of Schools Reporting 10% Illness" shows 2 schools statewide reaching that threshold this week, one in Polk County (Region 1-C) and one in Muscatine County (Region 6-E). Regions 2-NE, 3-NW, 4-SW, and 5-SE each reported 0 schools at the 10% illness threshold, indicating minimal school-level illness activity statewide.

================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Virus Survey (Other Pathogens) ================
This molecular survey tracks all respiratory pathogens with at least one positive this season, excluding influenza and COVID-19. For the current week, the highest raw positive count was Rhinovirus/Enterovirus at 257 positives (30.0% positivity), followed by RSV at 155 (6.9%), Parainfluenza virus at 104 (12.1%), HMPV at 83 (9.7%), and Adenovirus at 30 (3.5%). The weekly trend chart shows a single tall early-season stacked bar (week ending ~Oct 15, 2022) totaling roughly 630 positives, dominated by Rhinovirus/Enterovirus and RSV with smaller Parainfluenza, HMPV, and Adenovirus contributions. The pattern reflects typical early-autumn respiratory activity led by rhinovirus/enterovirus alongside rising RSV and parainfluenza, ahead of the winter influenza season.


================================================================================
END OF FILE

Iowa HHS — Iowa Respiratory Virus Surveillance Report
MMWR Week 41, October 9, 2022 - October 15, 2022 (Season 2022-2023)
Source: https://publications.iowa.gov/41824/1/63f442ed-6483-4cce-882f-1665a20863c1.pdf
================================================================================

Note: Published by the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services. Summaries
of each surveillance section, excluding the cover page and the "About the Data"
methods section. Figures and embedded data values are described in prose.


================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Survey - Influenza ================
Overall influenza activity was low at week 41, the first week of the 2022-2023 season. The molecular testing chart shows a single early-season bar near 0% Flu A positivity, and the antigen chart shows the first small Flu A uptick at the start of the season with Flu B near zero. The current-week regional table reports total molecular positivity of 0.1% Flu A and 0.0% Flu B across 3,430 tests, and antigen positivity of 3.2% Flu A and 0.0% Flu B across 190 tests. By region, molecular Flu A reached 0.6% in 2-NE (179 tests), 0.1% in 6-E (2,427 tests), and 0.0% in 1-C (768 tests) and 3-NW (56 tests); 4-SW reported no tests and 5-SE had 0 molecular tests. Antigen Flu A was highest in 5-SE-adjacent region 2-NE at 21.4% (14 tests), followed by 6-E at 10.0% (20 tests) and 1-C at 3.2% (77 tests), with 3-NW and 5-SE at 0.0%. The cover Quick Stats list molecular 0.1% and antigen 3.2% Flu Positive.

================ SECTION: International Influenza Activity (WHO) and National Influenza-Like Illness (CDC) ================
The WHO/GISRS FluNet map (generated 14 October 2022) shows the percentage of respiratory specimens testing positive for influenza by transmission zone, with elevated influenza positivity and A-predominant pie charts across parts of Central/South America, sub-Saharan Africa, and South/Southeast Asia, while much of North America and Europe showed lower positivity. The CDC ILINet activity map for the 2022-23 season, week 41 ending October 15, 2022, shows most states at Minimal or Low ILI activity (green shades), with notable early elevation in the South: Texas at Very High, Louisiana and South Carolina High, and Georgia and surrounding states Moderate, indicating early southern-state influenza-like illness activity.

================ SECTION: Influenza Testing at the State Hygienic Laboratory (SHL) ================
Cumulative influenza viruses detected by SHL (10/3/2021 - current week) totaled 2 Influenza A and 0 Influenza B at this early point in the season. Both were A(H3); there were no A(H1N1)pdm09, A not subtyped, or A Variant detections, consistent with the cover's "Predominant Flu at SHL: A(H3)." By age, the two A(H3) detections were one in the 65-and-over group and one in 50-64; all other age groups (0-4, 5-17, 18-24, 25-49, and Unknown) had zero. The weekly stacked chart shows a single early bar near 2 positives (dark red A(H3)) at the start of the season in October 2022, with no Influenza B (B Victoria, B Yamagata, or B not subtyped) detected.

================ SECTION: Outpatient Health Care Provider Surveillance Program (ILINet) ================
Outpatient ILI activity was low at the season's start. The seasonal ILI chart shows the 2022-23 curve (dark red) beginning near 0.8% for the week ending 10/15/2022, well below the high peaks of prior seasons. The recent-weeks table shows Week 39 (10/1/2022) 0.58% (27 total ILI), Week 40 (10/8/2022) 1.17% (52), and Week 41 (10/15/2022) 0.78% (37 total ILI), matching the cover Quick Stat of 0.78% Outpatient ILI. The current-week (week 41) age distribution was concentrated in ages 5-24 (11) and 25-49 (13), with 0-4 at 7, 65-and-older at 5, and 50-64 at 1.

================ SECTION: Influenza and COVID-19 Hospitalizations - HealthData.gov ================
Influenza hospitalizations were low at season start. The "Influenza Hospitalizations by Week - HHS Protect" chart shows 5 flu hospitalizations at all Iowa hospitals for the week ending 10/8/2022, rising to 7 for the current week ending 10/15/2022 (matching the cover Quick Stat of 7 flu hospitalizations at all Iowa hospitals). The cover also reports the sentinel rate at 2.186 per 10,000 and 0 cumulative flu deaths across all ages. The Iowa Sentinel Site survey (10/2/2022 - 10/15/2022) recorded 1 total influenza-associated hospitalization by age group, occurring entirely in the 5-24 age group, with 0-4, 25-49, 50-64, and 65+ each at 0.

================ SECTION: School Illness Reporting ================
School illness was low at week 41. The sentinel-school chart shows the 2022-23 percent-absent curve (purple) beginning at 2.7% absent for the week ending 10/15/2022, in range with prior early-season values. The county map of "Numbers of Schools Reporting 10% Illness" shows 2 schools statewide reaching that threshold this week (matching the cover Quick Stat of 2): one in Region 6-E (Iowa County area) and one in Region 5-SE (Des Moines County area). Regions 1-C, 2-NE, 3-NW, and 4-SW each reported 0 schools at the 10% illness threshold, indicating minimal school-level illness activity statewide at the start of the season.

================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Virus Survey (Other Pathogens) ================
This molecular survey tracks all respiratory pathogens with at least one positive this season (excluding influenza and COVID-19). For the current week, the highest positivity was Rhinovirus/Enterovirus at 32.0% (293 positives), followed by Parainfluenza virus at 12.6% (118), RSV at 9.6% (277), Adenovirus at 4.5% (42), and Coronavirus (not COVID-19) at 0.3% (3). The weekly stacked-bar trend chart shows a single tall early-season bar near 730 total positives for the week ending 10/15/2022, dominated by Rhinovirus/Enterovirus and RSV with smaller contributions from Parainfluenza virus, HMPV, Adenovirus, and Coronavirus, reflecting the typical fall rhinovirus/enterovirus and rising RSV burden as the respiratory season begins.


================================================================================
END OF FILE

Iowa HHS — Iowa Respiratory Virus Surveillance Report
MMWR Week 42, October 16, 2022 - October 22, 2022 (Season 2022-2023)
Source: https://publications.iowa.gov/41825/1/f55e80f1-64a0-4615-b3b4-829fba7c2a9b.pdf
================================================================================

Note: Published by the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services. Summaries
of each surveillance section, excluding the cover page and the "About the Data"
methods section. Figures and embedded data values are described in prose.


================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Survey - Influenza ================
Overall Iowa influenza activity was low at week 42 (week ending 10/22/2022), and A(H3) was the predominant flu detected at SHL. The molecular testing chart shows only early-season activity, with roughly 2,000-4,000 weekly tests in late October and near-zero positivity for both Flu A and Flu B; the antigen chart shows about 200-450 weekly tests with a small Flu A uptick and minimal Flu B. The current-week regional table reports total molecular positivity of 0.4% Flu A and 0.0% Flu B across 3,742 tests, and antigen positivity of 0.9% Flu A and 2.1% Flu B across 434 tests. By region, molecular Flu A positivity was highest in 3-NW at 0.8% (119 tests), with 1-C at 0.5% (1,003), 6-E at 0.4% (2,383), and 2-NE/4-SW at 0.0%; antigen Flu A reached 1.3% in 3-NW (230 tests) and 0.8% in 1-C (122), and antigen Flu B reached 2.6% in 3-NW and 2.5% in 1-C.

================ SECTION: International Influenza Activity (WHO) / National Influenza-Like Illness (CDC) ================
The WHO/GISRS FluNet map (generated 14 October 2022) shows the percentage of respiratory specimens testing positive for influenza by transmission zone, with pie charts depicting subtype mix (A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3), A not subtyped, and B) and positivity bins (0-10%, 11-20%, 21-30%, >30%); elevated positivity and substantial A(H3) and B circulation appear across parts of the Americas, Europe, Africa, and Asia, with several zones lacking sufficient data. The CDC national ILI activity map for the 2022-23 season week 42 (ending Oct 22, 2022) shows widespread early-season activity, with "Very High"/"High" ILI in the Southeast and South-Central states (including South Carolina, Georgia, Tennessee, Virginia, Texas, and the District of Columbia), "Moderate" levels in parts of the South and Northeast, and "Low"/"Minimal" activity across most of the Midwest, Plains, and West, including Iowa.

================ SECTION: Influenza Testing at the State Hygienic Laboratory (SHL) ================
Cumulative influenza viruses detected by SHL (10/3/2021 - current week) totaled only 4 Influenza A and 0 Influenza B this early in the season. All 4 were A(H3); there were no A(H1N1)pdm09, A not subtyped, or A Variant detections, and no B Victoria, B Yamagata, or B not subtyped. By age, A(H3) detections were distributed as 2 among ages 65 and over, and 1 each among ages 18-24 and 50-64, with 0 in the 0-4, 5-17, 25-49, and Unknown groups. The weekly stacked chart shows the first positives appearing around late October 2022 (near Nov 1, 2022), with one week reaching 2 A(H3) detections (dark red) and an adjacent week at 1, and no detections elsewhere in the season-to-date.

================ SECTION: Outpatient Health Care Provider Surveillance Program (ILINet) ================
Outpatient ILI activity was low at week 42. The seasonal ILI chart shows the 2022-23 curve (dark red) just beginning, with ILI at 1.2% for the week ending 10/22/2022, near the low early-season range of prior seasons. The recent-weeks table shows Week 40 (10/8/2022) at 1.17% (52 total ILI), Week 41 (10/15/2022) at 0.78% (37), and Week 42 (10/22/2022) at 1.21% (46 total ILI). The current-week age distribution was concentrated in ages 5-24 (25) and 0-4 (11), with 25-49 at 4, 50-64 at 3, and 65 and older at 3. The cover lists the outpatient ILI rate as 19.14 per 10,000.

================ SECTION: Influenza and COVID-19 Hospitalizations - HealthData.gov ================
Influenza hospitalizations were rising early in the season. The HHS Protect weekly chart shows Iowa hospital flu hospitalizations increasing from 5 the week of 10/8/2022 to 7 on 10/15/2022 and 10 for the current week of 10/22/2022. The Iowa Sentinel Site Survey of influenza-associated hospitalizations by age shows 0 the week of 10/8/2022, 1 (age 5-24) on 10/15/2022, and 3 on 10/22/2022, comprising 2 among ages 65+ and 1 among ages 0-4. The cover quick stats report 10 flu hospitalizations at all Iowa hospitals, a sentinel rate, and 0 cumulative flu deaths across all ages this season-to-date.

================ SECTION: School Illness Reporting ================
School illness was low at week 42. The sentinel-school chart shows the 2022-23 percent-absent curve (purple) just beginning near 2.5-3% in early weeks, with 3.2% of enrolled students absent due to illness for the week ending 10/22/2022, within range of prior seasons. The county map of "Numbers of Schools Reporting 10% Illness" shows 4 schools statewide reaching that threshold this week: 1 in Black Hawk County (6-E), 2 in Polk County (1-C), and 1 in Des Moines County (5-SE). Regions 2-NE, 3-NW, and 4-SW reported 0 schools at the 10% illness threshold, indicating minimal school-level illness activity statewide.

================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Virus Survey (Other Pathogens) ================
This molecular survey tracks all non-flu, non-COVID respiratory pathogens with at least one positive this season. For the current week, the highest positivity was Rhinovirus/Enterovirus at 28.1% (249 positives), followed by Parainfluenza virus at 15.7% (139), RSV at 14.1% (364), Adenovirus at 3.7% (33), HMPV at 0.2% (2), and Coronavirus (not COVID-19) at 0.1% (1). The weekly trend chart, which begins around mid-November 2022, shows Rhinovirus/Enterovirus highest near 28.1% and Parainfluenza virus and RSV elevated near 15-16% and 14%, respectively, reflecting an early-season fall mix dominated by rhinovirus/enterovirus, parainfluenza, and rising RSV ahead of the influenza season.


================================================================================
END OF FILE

Iowa HHS — Iowa Respiratory Virus Surveillance Report
MMWR Week 44, October 30, 2022 - November 5, 2022 (Season 2022-2023)
Source: https://publications.iowa.gov/41930/1/Flu%20Report%20week%2044%20increasing.pdf
================================================================================

Note: Published by the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services. Summaries
of each surveillance section, excluding the cover page and the "About the Data"
methods section. Figures and embedded data values are described in prose.


================ SECTION: International Influenza Activity Summary - WHO / National Influenza-Like Illness (CDC) ================
The WHO International Influenza Activity map (Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System / FluNet, generated 28 October 2022) shows the percentage of respiratory specimens testing positive for influenza by transmission zone, with pie charts colored by virus subtype (A H1N1 pdm09, A H3, A not subtyped, B). Influenza activity was widespread across the Northern Hemisphere temperate zones with A H3 predominating in many regions. The CDC National Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) map for the 2022-23 season, week 44 ending November 5, 2022, shows ILI activity levels concentrated in the South-Central and Southeastern United States, with several states (including the District of Columbia) at "Very High," neighboring states "High" to "Moderate," and much of the northern and western U.S. at "Low" to "Minimal," reflecting an unusually early and intense national flu season.

================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Survey - Influenza ================
Iowa influenza activity was increasing at week 44 and overall flu activity is classified as "Increasing." The molecular testing chart shows early-season Flu A positivity beginning to climb on roughly 2,000-5,000 weekly tests, while the antigen chart (up to ~440 tests/week) shows Flu A rising sharply to near 8% with Flu B near zero. For the current week, total molecular positivity was 2.3% Flu A and 0.0% Flu B across 4,651 tests, and total antigen positivity was 5.1% Flu A and 1.0% Flu B across 296 tests (cover quick stats list molecular 2.3% and antigen 6.1%). By region, molecular Flu A positivity was highest in 3-NW at 8.7% (333 tests) and 4-SW at 3.9% (77 tests), followed by 1-C 3.1% (1,195 tests), 6-E 1.2% (2,841 tests), and 2-NE 1.8% (168 tests); 5-SE was 0.0% (37 tests). Antigen Flu A positivity peaked in 2-NE at 11.1% (18 tests) and 1-C at 8.7% (126 tests), with antigen Flu B reaching 1.6% in both 1-C and 6-E.

================ SECTION: Influenza Testing at the State Hygienic Laboratory (SHL) ================
Cumulative influenza viruses detected by SHL (10/3/2021 - current week) totaled 21 Influenza A and 0 Influenza B. Influenza A H3 dominated with 17 detections and A H1N1 pdm09 had 4, with none A-not-subtyped; A H3 is the predominant flu at SHL. By age, the highest A totals were among 0-4 (7), then 5-17 (4), 18-24 (3), 65 and over (3), and 2 each for 25-49 and 50-64. The weekly stacked chart shows the season's first positives emerging in late October/early November 2022, peaking near 13 the most recent week (a mix of A H3 in red and A H1N1 pdm09 in teal), consistent with the early A H3-driven start to the 2022-23 season. No Influenza B (Vic or Yam) had been detected.

================ SECTION: Outpatient Health Care Provider Surveillance Program (ILINet) ================
Outpatient ILI activity was elevated early for the season and above the regional baseline. The seasonal ILI chart shows the 2022-23 curve (dark red) climbing steeply through weeks 41-44 to 2.9% for the week ending 11/5/2022, tracking well above most prior seasons at this point in the year. The current-week age distribution (week 44, 11/5/2022) totaled 107 ILI cases for an ILI percent of 2.92%, concentrated in ages 5-24 (58) and 25-49 (19), with 0-4 at 15, 65 and older at 9, and 50-64 at 6. The cumulative flu vaccination chart shows the 2022-23 season (teal) plateauing near 25% by November, below the 2019-20, 2020-21, and 2021-22 seasons (~34-40% eventual coverage).

================ SECTION: Influenza and COVID-19 Hospitalizations - HealthData.gov ================
Influenza hospitalizations at all Iowa hospitals (HHS Protect) rose steadily through October into early November 2022: 5 (10/8), 7 (10/15), 10 (10/22), about 19-20 (10/29 peak), and 16 for the current week ending 11/5/2022 (the week 44 quick stat reports 16 flu hospitalizations and 0 cumulative flu deaths all ages). The Iowa Sentinel Site Survey of influenza-associated hospitalizations by age group shows a small weekly count rising to 4 total for the week ending 11/5/2022 (the sentinel quick stat reports a rate of 8.123/10,000), with 65+ (teal) consistently dominant (2) plus contributions from 50-64 and 5-24; the 10/22 week showed 3 driven by 65+ and a 0-4 case, reflecting the early-season climb in influenza hospitalizations among older Iowans.

================ SECTION: School Illness Reporting ================
School illness was rising early in the season at week 44. The sentinel-school chart shows the 2022-23 percent-absent curve (purple) climbing through weeks 41-44 to 3.2% absent due to illness for the week ending 11/5/2022, above several prior seasons at this point. The county map of "Numbers of Schools Reporting 10% Illness" shows 11 schools statewide reaching that threshold this week (matching the quick stat of 11), distributed across regions: 3-NW had schools in Plymouth, Buena Vista, and Audubon areas; 1-C had Marshall (2) and Webster/Black Hawk-adjacent counties; 6-E had Linn, Iowa, and Johnson; 4-SW had Montgomery; and 5-SE had Wapello and Muscatine, indicating broad but modest early school-level illness activity statewide.

================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Virus Survey (Other Pathogens) ================
This molecular survey tracks all respiratory pathogens with at least one positive this season (excluding influenza and COVID-19). For the current week, RSV was highest in volume with 810 positives at 20.5% positivity, followed by Rhinovirus/Enterovirus with 304 positives at 23.8% (the highest positivity percent), Parainfluenza virus 141 positives at 11.0%, Adenovirus 69 positives at 5.4%, HMPV 5 positives at 0.4%, and Coronavirus (not COVID-19) 2 positives at 0.2%. The weekly trend chart shows RSV (teal) surging upward toward 20.5% in late October/early November 2022 while Rhinovirus/Enterovirus (brown), which began the season above 30%, declined toward 23.8%, reflecting an early and intense RSV wave concurrent with the rising influenza season.


================================================================================
END OF FILE

================================================================================

Note: Published by the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services. Summaries
of each surveillance section, excluding the cover page and the "About the Data"
methods section. Figures and embedded data values are described in prose.


================ SECTION: International Influenza Activity Summary (WHO) and National Influenza-Like Illness (CDC) ================
The WHO/GISRS FluNet world map (generated 11 November 2022) shows the percentage of respiratory specimens testing positive for influenza by transmission zone, with pie wedges indicating subtype mix (A H1N1 pdm09, A H3, A not subtyped, B). Many zones across South America, sub-Saharan Africa, South and Southeast Asia, and Oceania showed elevated positivity (often 11-25% or higher), with A H3 and A not subtyped predominating in the Northern Hemisphere zones while parts of the tropics showed mixed A/B activity. The CDC national ILI activity map for the 2022-23 season, week 46 ending 11/19/2022, showed widespread "Very High" ILI activity across the southern, south-central, and eastern United States (dark red), with much of the South, mid-Atlantic, and Northeast at the highest levels, while a handful of western and northern states registered Moderate to Minimal activity, reflecting an unusually early and intense national influenza season.

================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Survey - Influenza ================
Iowa influenza activity was Moderate at week 46 and rising sharply. The molecular testing chart shows Flu A positivity climbing steeply through November 2022 on roughly 5,000-7,000 weekly tests, with Flu B remaining at 0%. The antigen chart shows Flu A rising toward ~13-14% on ~380-600 weekly tests, with Flu B low. The current-week regional table reports total molecular positivity of 7.6% Flu A and 0.0% Flu B across 6,653 tests, and antigen positivity of 12.3% Flu A and 1.3% Flu B across 383 tests. Region 3-NW had the highest molecular Flu A positivity at 16.8% (552 tests), followed by 1-C at 11.6% (1,488 tests); antigen Flu A reached 14.0% in both 1-C (186 tests) and 2-NE (43 tests), with antigen Flu B at 2.3% in 2-NE. Region 4-SW reported 142 molecular tests (9.2% positive) but no antigen tests.

================ SECTION: Influenza Testing at the State Hygienic Laboratory (SHL) ================
Cumulative influenza viruses detected by SHL (10/3/2021 - current week) totaled 56 Influenza A and 0 Influenza B. Influenza A H3 dominated with 36 detections, A H1N1 pdm09 had 16, and 4 were not subtyped. By age, the highest A totals were among 5-17 (20) and 18-24 (10), followed by 25-49 (8), 0-4 (9), 50-64 (6), and 65+ (3); 9 were of unknown age. The weekly stacked chart shows positives rising rapidly in November 2022 to a current peak near 21 results in the latest week, composed mostly of A H3 (red) with A H1N1 pdm09 (teal) and a small A not subtyped (orange) sliver appearing in the most recent week; no Flu B (B Vic or B Yam) had been detected this season.

================ SECTION: Outpatient Health Care Provider Surveillance Program (ILINet) ================
Outpatient ILI activity was rising at week 46. The seasonal ILI chart shows the 2022-23 curve (dark brown) climbing from ~1% in early autumn to 3.3% for the week ending 11/19/2022, an early-season rise relative to prior seasons. The current-week age distribution table reports 153 total ILI cases for an ILI percent of 3.34%, concentrated in ages 5-24 (74) and 0-4 (41), with 25-49 (22), 65+ (10), and 50-64 (6). The cumulative flu-vaccine chart shows 2022-23 uptake (teal) plateauing near 27% by November, tracking below the 2019-2020 (~40%), 2020-2021 (~38%), and 2021-2022 (~34%) season curves at comparable points.

================ SECTION: Influenza and COVID-19 Hospitalizations - HealthData.gov ================
Influenza hospitalizations at all Iowa hospitals (HHS Protect) rose steadily through autumn, increasing from 5 the week of 10/8/2022 to 31 for the week ending 11/19/2022 (the week 46 quick stat reports 31 flu hospitalizations), the season high to date. The sentinel-site survey of voluntarily reporting hospitals shows influenza-associated hospitalizations by age climbing to 18 for the week ending 11/26/2022, dominated by the 65+ group (~9), with 50-64 (~3), 25-49 (~2), and 5-24 (~4) contributing; the sentinel rate quick stat was 12.07 per 10,000. Cumulative influenza deaths across all ages remained at 0 for the season.

================ SECTION: School Illness Reporting ================

================ SECTION: Quick Stats for Week 11 ================
Overall influenza activity was MODERATE. Lab survey flu PCR positivity was 22.1% (up from 0.7% a year prior), predominant SHL flu virus was B Vic, and outpatient ILI was 4.2%, well above the 2.0% regional baseline. Long-term care flu outbreaks remained elevated and flu deaths nonzero (2 noted); flu hospitalizations were 100 (up from 7 a year earlier). COVID-19 activity was VERY LOW: lab survey COVID PCR positivity 3.3% (down from 14.2%), predominant lineage JN.1, ER visits 0.7%, COVID hospitalizations 48 (down from 211), and 4 COVID deaths. Among other respiratory viruses, Influenza led at 22.1%, Rhinovirus/Enterovirus 13.3%, non-COVID Coronavirus 7.9%.

================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Survey - Influenza ================
The molecular testing chart shows influenza at or near its late-season peak, highly elevated by week ending 3/16/24, with both Flu A and B contributing. Antigen testing showed a similarly elevated tail. For the current week (molecular only), Iowa logged 954 flu positives out of 4,307 tests for an overall 22.1% positivity. By Preparedness Service Area, rates ranged from 11.1% (area 7) to 31.0% (area 3, 157 of 506); area 6 had the most positives (440 of 1,691, 26.0%), area 1A had 204 of 1,150 (17.7%), area 2 reached 26.7% (39 of 146), and area 5 had 84 of 647 (13.0%).

================ SECTION: Influenza testing at the State Hygienic Laboratory (SHL) ================
Cumulative influenza viruses detected by SHL since 10/1/2023 totaled 335 influenza A (151 A H3, 11 A not subtyped, 173 A(H1N1)pdm09) and 194 influenza B (6 B not subtyped, 188 B Vic, 0 B Yam). For the current week, SHL detected 5 influenza A positives (all A(H1N1)pdm09) and 6 influenza B (all B Vic). The weekly bar chart shows positives surged through January-March 2024, with B Vic (blue) and A(H1N1)pdm09 (gold) dominating the late-season peaks (often 25-35 per week) and remaining elevated near 11 in the current week. Only Iowa residents are included; "not subtyped" specimens may be pending or weakly positive.

================ SECTION: Outpatient Health Care Provider Surveillance Program (ILINET) ================
The 2023-24 ILI curve (dark red) rose to about 5.0% around weeks 6-7 (early 2024) and remained well above the 2.0% regional baseline at roughly 4.2% by week 11, reflecting a late-season resurgence. The age-group table for the past four weeks shows ILI percent of 5.11% (week 8), 3.70% (week 9), 3.91% (week 10), and 4.19% (week 11). In week 11, total ILI was 149 visits, distributed as 24 in ages 0-4, 68 in ages 5-24, 38 in ages 25-49, 7 in ages 50-64, and 12 in ages 65+, with the 5-24 age group driving most of the elevated ILI.

================ SECTION: Hospitalizations ================
Per HealthData.gov, influenza hospitalizations at Iowa hospitals (52-week view) climbed through late winter to peak around 180 per week in early March 2024, and remained high at about 100 by week ending 3/16/24. COVID-19 hospitalizations, broken out by age group, peaked near 405 per week in late December 2023, with the oldest age bands (70-79 and 80+, orange/teal) contributing the largest shares; weekly counts fell to roughly 48 by mid-March 2024, indicating COVID-19 hospitalization burden had declined sharply while influenza hospitalizations remained near their seasonal peak.

================ SECTION: School Illness ================
The sentinel school absenteeism chart plots percent of enrolled students absent due to illness across seasons; the 2023-24 line (dark red) tracked among the higher seasons in winter, peaking near 6.5% around weeks 1-3, then easing but remaining elevated relative to most seasons into March. The county map ("Number of Schools Reporting 10% Illness by County - Current Week") shows scattered schools meeting the 10% threshold (e.g., Pottawattamie, Jackson, Appanoose). By Preparedness Region, area 1C reported 2 schools, with areas 4 and 5 each reporting 1, for a statewide total of 4 schools.

================ SECTION: Iowa Syndromic Surveillance Program ================
The ER visit chart for respiratory syndromes (since Jan 2023) shows COVID-19 (blue) peaking around 6.0% in late December 2023, while Flu (gold) peaked later near 5.5% around late February/early March 2024; RSV (green) peaked near 2.0%. By week ending 3/16/24 Flu was still notably elevated near 4.2% while COVID and RSV had fallen to near 0.7-0.8%. The inpatient visit chart shows a similar picture: COVID-19 peaked highest (~6.3% in late December 2023), with Flu peaking later (~3.2%) and RSV lower; Flu remained the most elevated syndrome near 2.4% by mid-March as the other syndromes eased toward baseline.

================ SECTION: Iowa Respiratory Virus Survey ================
This pathogen-group survey (molecular only) shows percent positive by week and for the current week. For week ending 3/16/24, Influenza led at 22.1%, Rhinovirus/Enterovirus at 13.3%, non-COVID Coronavirus 7.9%, RSV 5.5%, COVID-19 3.3%, HMPV 2.7%, Parainfluenza virus 2.7%, and Adenovirus lowest at 2.4%. The trend chart shows Rhinovirus/Enterovirus persistently dominant for much of the year, but a teal pathogen (influenza) surged to ~28% in late winter and remained the top pathogen this week. The top-5 sparkline panel highlights Influenza, Rhinovirus/Enterovirus, non-COVID Coronavirus, RSV, and COVID-19 as the leading groups currently.
